title: VP Staff Pocket Notes — pre-exec sync and follow-ups
body:
Quick pocket notes for tomorrow's 30m VP/staff sync — raw + messy. Use as speaking crib sheet and checklist for follow-ups.

High-level objective: align on capacity & risk, sign off on 1-week runway for Dedicated burst plan, confirm exec asks for the account escalations (ACME & FinServe). End with clear owners and deadlines.

Toplines to say: 
- Dedicated utilization steady but trending up 6% w/w; predicted saturation if burst not approved by next Tue (see INF-3421).
- Latency P95 on hosted api spiked last Wed due to prefix-cache miss — mitigation landed but need permanent caching policy (PR #1284).
- Customer impact: ACME had 8% error-rate during 09:00–11:00 PST on Mar 9; CS has tentative credit ask.

Agenda (30m):
1) 3 min quick numbers — PV/Capacity/Cost (Aisha)
2) 8 min incident recap & mitigation status (Ethan)
3) 8 min Dedicated burst proposal + approval ask (me)
4) 6 min key customer escalations + proposed comms (Daniel)
5) 5 min decisions & owners + unblock list

Notes & talking points (bulletified):
- Numbers: call out Dedicated pool avg util 78% vs target 70%; burst capacity would add +20% for 48h after approval. Cost vs SLA: incremental monthly cost ~$12k but prevents estimated $200k churn risk.
- Incident: root cause = stale KV-cache eviction interaction with new batching heuristic; hotfix rolled (serving-runtime PR 1284) — ask: can we fast-track full regression test and merge by EOD Fri? QA needs two runs; SRE wants 1 smoke deploy to canary region first.
- Customer comms: draft apology + mitigation note ready in drive (linked). Recommend offering ACME 5% service credit + 1-2hr tech review session w/solutions eng.
- Risk: Private deployments pipeline still missing hardened KMS rotation automation — flagged to security. If any large enterprise contract in next 30d, we need a plan B.

Decisions to request from staff (explicit):
- Approve temporary burst for Dedicated for up to 72h (owner: Monica) — yes/no in this meeting.
- Greenlight expedited regression test (owner: Eng QE lead — Daniel to call).
- Approve customer credit authority up to $15k for CS to resolve ACME (owner: VP CS — Aisha).

Open questions / things to surface during meeting:
- Do we formally escalate to CTO for procurement of extra GPUs if burst is insufficient? (cost justification ready if needed)
- Are there downstream billing impacts for customers on reserved vs hosted that we need to flag?
- Do we want to temporarily relax auto-scaling min for a small pool to reduce cold-starts?

Action items (short-labeled, owner, ETA):
- Monica: Send formal burst approval email + signal to infra-provisioning (by 2026-03-13 18:00)
- Daniel: Kick off expedited QA runs for PR #1284 and post status to #exec-ops (by 2026-03-14 morning)
- Aisha: Draft ACME comms + proposed credit figure and publish to CS leadership for sign-off (by 2026-03-13 20:00)
- Ethan: Prepare incident postmortem outline and timeline for full RCA (by 2026-03-16)
- Eng SRE (TBD): Toggle canary pool and run smoke deploy once PR merged (ETA depends on QA)

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep the ask simple: 'short burst now, planning for 6-week capacity increase if usage holds'. Avoid deep infra cost math in meeting; have numbers ready if asked.
- If anyone pushes back on credits, propose credit + technical review combo (reduces churn risk).
- Watch for 'long tail' questions about Private KMS — say: security owns roadmap, we have a mitigation plan but not GA.

Follow-up template to send immediately after meeting (copy + paste):
Subject: VP Staff Sync — decisions & owners (Mar 13)
Body:
- Approved: temporary Dedicated burst (owner: Monica) — provisioning team to start once funds cleared.
- Action: Daniel to run expedited QA on PR #1284 (ETA: Mar 14 AM).
- Action: Aisha to finalize ACME comms + credit proposal (ETA: Mar 13 20:00).
- Action: Ethan to circulate incident PM template and target RCA date (ETA: Mar 16).
Please reply if any ETA needs adjusting.

References / quick links (for Qs in meeting):
- Incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Serving+Runtime+Incidents
- PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/1284
- Ticket: JIRA-INF-3421 (Dedicated burst request)
- CS draft: drive:/shared/CS/ACME/communications/draft-0309.md

Random scratch bits (do not read aloud unless needed):
- If they ask about longer-term procurement: show 12-month runway with usage scenarios (simple chart I can share after).
- If CFO asks about cost: highlight unit economics improvement from caching + batching optimizations, hitting target TCO in Q3.

End. Keep this doc as ephemeral scratch — I'll prune and move final follow-ups to shared_drives/company/memos once actions are locked.

-- M
